title: My Calendar I
statement:
Build a class `MyCalendar` that stores events and refuses any new event that would clash with one it already holds. An event given by `startTime` and `endTime` is the half-open range `[startTime, endTime)`: it contains every real moment `x` with `startTime <= x < endTime`, so it includes its start but not its end. Two events clash when at least one moment lies in both.

- `MyCalendar()` creates a calendar with no events.
- `book(startTime, endTime)` checks the new event against every stored event. If it clashes with none, the event is stored and the call returns `true`. Otherwise the call returns `false` and the calendar stays as it was.
constraints: At most 1000 calls are made to book
notes:
## Intuition

Accepted events never overlap each other, so sorted by start they also end in order. A new event can only clash with its two neighbours in that order: the first stored event that starts at or after `startTime`, and the stored event just before it. Binary search finds that spot in O(log n). The brute force compares the new event with every stored one, which is O(n) per call.

## Approach

1. Keep `bookings`, the accepted events as `[start, end]` pairs sorted by start.
2. In `book`, binary search with `left` and `right` for the first index whose start is not below `startTime`.
3. If the event at `left` starts before `endTime`, the new event runs into it: return `false`.
4. If the event at `left - 1` ends after `startTime`, it runs into the new event: return `false`.
5. Otherwise insert the new pair at `left`, which keeps the list sorted, and return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

- `book(10, 20)`: `bookings` is empty, so `left = 0` has no neighbours. Store `[10, 20]` and return `true`.
- `book(15, 25)`: `10 < 15`, so `left = 1`. There is nothing at index 1, but the left neighbour `[10, 20]` ends at 20, after 15. Return `false`.
- `book(20, 30)`: again `left = 1`. The left neighbour ends at 20, which is not after 20, because ends are excluded. Store `[20, 30]` and return `true`.

The output is `[null, true, false, true]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log n) to find the spot plus O(n) for the array insertion, so O(n) per call and O(n²) for n calls; a balanced tree would make each call O(log n).
- Space: O(n) for the stored events.

## Pitfalls

- Ends are excluded: `[10, 20)` and `[20, 30)` do not clash, so compare with `<` and `>`, not `<=` and `>=`.
- Checking only the right neighbour misses an earlier event that is long enough to reach past `startTime`.
- A refused event must not be stored, or later calls will be judged against it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bookings` | accepted events as `[start, end]`, sorted by start |
| `left`, `right` | binary-search bounds; `left` ends at the insertion index |
| `mid` | the middle index being tested |
